headline: Hacker uses AI agents to breach 100 sites
dek: Norforge found the campaign while scanning exposed Cairn instances, according to The Verge.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A campaign with little oversight
body: A hacker breached more than 100 company sites with AI agents, according to Norforge, cited by The Verge and TechRadar.
Reuters confirmed victims such as John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins, TechRadar reports.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How the agents worked
s3.body: According to The Verge and TechRadar:

points.t: Short instructions in Chinese were enough (The Verge).
They tried SQL injection and file uploads (TechRadar).
Each attack took 23 hours on average (The Verge).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Cairn at the center
body: Cairn is an open-source platform where a user sets only a start and an end, per The Verge.
Its creator says misuse is a human decision, not a feature of the engine (The Verge).

stat.cap: per attack on average, The Verge says

items.t: No sign sensitive data was accessed, the company says.
The flaw hit a standalone site and was contained.
It is probing a possible attack on a vendor site.

caption.hook: A hacker used AI agents to breach more than 100 company sites, according to Norforge.
body: According to Norforge, cited by The Verge and TechRadar, the campaign surfaced on exposed instances of Cairn, an open-source platform for AI agents. Reuters confirmed victims such as John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins.

The Verge says each attack took 23 hours on average and that Norforge found more than 20 likely malicious instances. Cairn's creator says misuse is a human decision. John Deere and SharkNinja say they contained the issue.
caption.cta: Should open-source AI agent tools come with built-in safeguards?
